# Independent Hyperliquid signing fixtures

`official-sdk-vectors.json` is generated by the official Hyperliquid Python SDK,
not by Vault's Go implementation. All keys, addresses and actions are test data;
the public upstream test key must never hold assets. Every nonce and expiry is
intentionally historical. No action was submitted to an exchange.

The fixture records its SDK commit, source file hashes, package versions, and
the SHA-256 of the downloaded source archive. The SDK is MIT licensed; its notice
is preserved in `hyperliquid-sdk-LICENSE.txt`.

- SDK commit: [`2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0`](https://github.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyperliquid-python-sdk/tree/2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0)
- [Official signing implementation](https://github.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyperliquid-python-sdk/blob/2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0/hyperliquid/utils/signing.py)
- [Official action construction](https://github.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyperliquid-python-sdk/blob/2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0/hyperliquid/exchange.py)
- [Official exchange wire formats](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint)

## Reproduce

Use a disposable Python environment. Download the pinned source archive from
`https://codeload.github.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyperliquid-python-sdk/tar.gz/2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0`,
verify SHA-256
`e48dff272dbb1a021177d0a7e3f0be092665f060ec6a6b3224c3f51b47c43896`,
and install the archive with these signing dependencies:

```sh
python -m pip install ./sdk.tar.gz eth-account==0.13.7 eth-utils==5.3.1 msgpack==1.1.1
python scripts/test-hyperliquid-vectors.py
```

The generator checks installed SDK source hashes and package versions, rejects
network connections through a Python audit hook, and accepts no private key or
exchange URL. `--write` regenerates the fixture JSON after a deliberate review.

## Fixture schema and interpretation

Each vector contains `name`, `scheme` (`l1` or `user`), `network` (`mainnet` or
`testnet`), `signerAddress`, `input`, `digest`, and `signature` (`r`, `s`, `v`).
`input` is the exact exchange envelope before adding a signature: `action`,
`nonce`, and optional `vaultAddress` / `expiresAfter`. User actions already
contain `signatureChainId` and `hyperliquidChain`. L1 vectors also record
`msgpack` and `actionHash` to localize encoding differences.

The signing digest is extracted from the exact EIP-191 `SignableMessage` passed
by the SDK to `eth-account`; every signature is independently recovered to the
fixture address. Mainnet and testnet are covered for every action. L1 cases
cover the Cartesian product of absent/present vault and absent/present expiry.
These vectors establish encoding compatibility, not exchange acceptance or
whether an action is appropriate for a real account.

Field order matters for L1 MessagePack. The JSON action objects retain the SDK's
insertion order. Order encoding uses `a,b,p,s,r,t[,c]`; trigger details use
`isMarket,triggerPx,tpsl`; builder details use `b,f`. Missing optional fields are
omitted, not encoded as `null`. Positive and negative isolated-margin values
exercise the MessagePack integer representation. Monetary values remain decimal
strings. Do not pass the fixture through a JSON-to-`float64` conversion or sort
its action fields before generating MessagePack.

Single `modify` and TWAP action shapes follow the official API documentation;
the pinned SDK has no corresponding high-level TWAP method, so its generic
`sign_l1_action` computes those reference signatures. User signatures use the
SDK's action-specific functions, with the fixed SDK chain metadata. No unsigned
vault or expiry decoration is added to user actions. SDK `r` and `s` values are
hexadecimal integers and may omit leading zeroes; compare their integer value
when an implementation chooses fixed-width hex output.
